display.purpose: Song title, section names, dialog headings — the identity face; self-hosted.

body.purpose: All interactive UI text: buttons, nav, labels, comments.

label.purpose: Tuning readout, song metadata, measure-line labels.

mono.purpose: Every tab-grid cell value, note names, BPM — anything that is data, not prose.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Centered dialogs (Tuning Editor) over a black/70 scrim.

motion.name: playhead-glide
motion.purpose: The playhead overlay translates across the active line instead of jump-cutting cell to cell.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default hover/focus transition for ghost buttons, cell focus, tab underlines.

components.name: Primary Button (Play)
components.description: The transport's default play action — the only routinely-visible solid-crimson button in the system.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary"><svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 2.5 L13 8 L4 13.5 Z"/></svg> Play</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #d65a48; color: #171511; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; padding: 8px 24px; border: none; border-radius: 0; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary .ds-icon { width: 1em; height: 1em; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #d65a48; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The default UI button everywhere outside the transport: toolbar, section nav, track tabs, sidebar actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #9aa7b0; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; padding: 10px 12px; border: none; border-bottom: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #ece6d8; border-bottom-color: #4c4638; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #d65a48; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Danger Ghost Button
components.description: Clear / remove-track / remove-section / delete-song — same ghost shape, hovers to crimson instead of ink.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: transparent; color: #9aa7b0; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; padding: 10px 12px; border: none; border-bottom: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { color: #d65a48; border-bottom-color: rgba(214,90,72,0.4); } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #d65a48; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Underline Text Field
components.description: The system's only text-input style: no box, a hairline underline that turns crimson on focus. Used for song title, section names, comments, BPM, lyrics.
components.css: .ds-field { background: transparent; color: #ece6d8; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 13px; padding: 4px 6px; border: none; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a352c; border-radius: 0; outline: none; transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-field::placeholder { color: #9c9382; } .ds-field:hover { border-bottom-color: #4c4638; } .ds-field:focus { border-bottom-color: #d65a48; }

components.name: Track Tab (Navigation)
components.description: Instrument switcher: one system on screen at a time. Active tab gets a crimson underline and a raised-plate wash.
components.css: .ds-tab { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 6px 10px 6px 10px; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; color: #9aa7b0; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tab:hover { background: rgba(32,29,24,0.6); } .ds-tab-active { border-bottom-color: #d65a48; background: #201d18; color: #ece6d8; font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Card / Panel
components.description: The system's only container style: flat plate background, single hairline border, square corners, no shadow at rest.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: #171511; border: 1px solid #4c4638; border-radius: 0; padding: 20px; color: #ece6d8; }

components.name: Toast
components.description: Bottom-centered ephemeral confirmation, the one place a floating shadow appears outside modals/popovers.
components.css: .ds-toast { position: fixed; bottom: 80px; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); background: #ece6d8; color: #171511; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: 0 6px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.4); }

components.name: Transport Bar (signature)
components.description: Fixed bottom playback bar, Songsterr idiom: click-to-seek crimson scrub rule above centered transport controls and a BPM field.
components.css: .ds-transport { position: fixed; bottom: 0; left: 0; right: 0; background: #201d18; border-top: 1px solid #4c4638; } .ds-scrub { height: 6px; background: #171511; cursor: pointer; } .ds-scrub-fill { height: 100%; background: #d65a48; transition: width 0.1s linear; } .ds-transport-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 16px; padding: 10px 20px; max-width: 1100px; margin: 0 auto; position: relative; } .ds-bpm { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-size: 13px; color: #9aa7b0; position: absolute; right: 20px; }

components.name: Playhead Overlay (signature)
components.description: A single translating overlay per visible score line — a crimson left border with tinted fill — that glides (150ms ease-out) across cells during playback instead of jump-cutting per-cell borders.
components.css: .ds-line { position: relative; } .ds-playhead { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; border-left: 2px solid #d65a48; background: rgba(214,90,72,0.1); transition: left 0.15s ease-out; pointer-events: none; }

narrative.overview: The song is not a spreadsheet of cells with a toolbar floating above it; it is a blackened engraving plate under a raking work light, and the tab is the score etched into it. The metal ground is near-black and warm, the staff lines are hairline scores in the plate, and note values sit in the grid like struck type. One color is allowed to move under it — crimson — reserved for the transport and for the state that is actively happening: the focused cell, the playhead, the primary action. Everything else on the plate is ink, in three weights of legibility (full, soft/slate for secondary state, faint for tertiary), never a second hue competing for attention. This world shipped dark-only by explicit direction mid-build — it began as a light ivory-paper rendition and was deliberately flipped and committed as the sole mode, not a theme variant sitting alongside a light default. There is no light-mode fallback to design around; color-scheme: dark is asserted at the HTML root. Corners are square everywhere (border-radius: 0 !important is a project-wide reset), consistent with engraving in metal: nothing here is molded or soft-edged.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black warm metal ground, light-etched ink text, one crimson accent used sparingly for transport and active-state
Bodoni Moda (display/identity) + Inter (UI text) + JetBrains Mono (the grid itself and all numeric/note data)
Square corners everywhere, hairline dividers instead of cards or shadows for structure
A single floating corner widget (reference video) and a single fixed bottom transport bar are the only two elements that leave the document flow
Authored stroke-SVG icons for UI chrome; genuine music notation (repeat marks, tie mark) is drawn in literal Unicode glyphs as earned notation, not decoration

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Crimson appears only on the actively playing/selected/focused element or a destructive action's hover state — never as a static brand color splashed on chrome. If nothing is active, nothing on screen is crimson except the transport play button.

rules.name: The Three-Ink Rule
rules.body: Text uses exactly three weights of the same ink hue family (full ink, soft slate, faint) to express hierarchy — never a fourth neutral, never a tint of the accent for text color.

rules.name: The Grid-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything living inside the editable tab grid (fret numbers, note names, BPM) is JetBrains Mono; nothing outside the grid is set in the mono face for body text. Monospace signals "this is data you edit," never decoration.

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: Surfaces at rest are flat; a shadow appears only when an element has actually left the document flow (modal, popover, floating widget, toast) to signal "this is above the plate," never as ambient polish on ordinary panels or cards.

dos: Do keep crimson to the actively-playing/focused/selected element and destructive hover states only — see The One Accent Rule.
Do use JetBrains Mono for anything inside the editable grid (fret numbers, note names, BPM) and reserve it for that role.
Do use square corners everywhere; the global border-radius: 0 !important reset is a committed identity trait of this world, not a temporary default.

Do express depth with hairline borders and plate/plate-raised/plate-sunken tonal steps before reaching for a shadow; reserve shadows for elements that have actually left document flow (modal, popover, floating widget, toast).

Do keep the utility bar (add-measure/section, instrument tabs, section jump) pinned/sticky above the scrolling score — this was a direct build-time fix for controls that "don't move with the page," not optional chrome.
Do author new UI iconography as consistent-stroke SVGs matching Icons.tsx's 1.6px stroke convention; do not reach for bare Unicode glyphs for generic chrome.
donts: Don't introduce a second saturated accent color; the system's entire expressive color budget is one crimson against warm neutrals.
Don't round any corner; there is no exception in the shipped system, including modals and floating widgets.
Don't add drop shadows to elements that stay in normal document flow (cards, panels, buttons at rest) — shadow is reserved for genuinely floating/overlay elements per The Flat Plate Rule.

Don't stack more than one instrument track's grid on screen at once; the one-system-at-a-time rule (switched by track tab) is a structural invariant of the score metaphor, not a space-saving default that can be relaxed.
